title: Localizations of Noetherian rings are Noetherian
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in S$, $st\in S$ for $s,t\in S$). Let $\varphi:R\to R'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings that is a localization of $R$ at $S$: (a) $\varphi(s)$ is a unit of $R'$ for every $s\in S$; (b) every element of $R'$ is $\varphi(r)\varphi(s)^{-1}$ for some $r\in R$, $s\in S$; (c) $\varphi(r)=0$ implies $sr=0$ for some $s\in S$ (for instance $R'=S^{-1}R$, the ring of fractions $r/s$, with $r\mapsto r/1$). Then $R'$ is a Noetherian ring.
